purpose: BabelBrain connects 3D Slicer trajectories and anatomical images to a separately installed focused-ultrasound simulation application and imports its results. It is intended for researchers planning and inspecting transcranial ultrasound simulations.
summary: The extension has clear documentation, a BSD license, and a mock-based self-test, but its file handling can overwrite existing images and expose subject-related paths and trajectory data to other local users. The supplied source was inspected, but the catalog branch and exact commit could not be independently resolved. 🔴 Do not merge yet: fix the unintended overwrite and shared-file privacy issues, and verify the catalog revision.

safety.rationale: Inspected launch, T1 export, JSON synchronization and subprocess handling in BabelBrain.py and SyncProtocol.py. An export can overwrite an existing image without confirmation, and the synchronization file is explicitly made world-readable on POSIX systems.

environment.rationale: Inspected module imports, both CMake files and subprocess launch. The extension does not install packages or modify Slicer's shared Python environment; it launches the separately installed application with the startup environment.

packaging.rationale: The module CMake file lists its imported Python files and icon, and EXTENSION_DEPENDS matches the empty catalog dependencies. The tools cannot independently resolve the catalog's main branch, verify the supplied commit, or build the extension.

license.rationale: LICENSE grants BSD 3-Clause redistribution permission. README describes the separately installed BabelBrain as BSD-3; that separate application's repository and release contents were not independently inspected.

soundness.rationale: Inspected the parameter handling, geometry checks, result loading and included mock test. Existing geometry mismatch warnings are displayed only after the external application has already been launched.

utility.rationale: README provides prerequisites, usage, tests, citation and a research-only disclaimer; BabelBrain.py includes a mock end-to-end test. Tests and the real simulation workflow were not run.

findings.title: T1 export can overwrite an existing image without confirmation
findings.evidence:
if header is None or header["affine"] is None:
            name = SP.MakeTargetNames([volumeNode.GetName()])[0]
            fname = os.path.join(outputPath, name + "_T1w.nii.gz")
            slicer.util.exportNode(volumeNode, fname)
            header = SP.ReadNiftiHeader(fname)
findings.explanation: When a modified volume or non-NIfTI input is run, the extension exports it to a predictable name in the selected output directory without checking whether that file already exists. An existing image at that path, potentially another subject's scan or an earlier version, can be overwritten before the later warning is shown.
findings.suggestion: Use a unique filename or explicitly check for an existing destination and obtain informed confirmation before replacing it.

findings.title: Synchronization input can disclose subject data to other local users
findings.evidence:
os.makedirs(dirname, exist_ok=True)
    fd, tmpname = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=dirname, prefix=".tmp_", suffix=".json")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
        os.chmod(tmpname, 0o644)
        os.replace(tmpname, fname)
findings.explanation: On a shared POSIX computer, when the home directory and newly created sync directory are traversable by other users, mode 0644 lets those users read the input JSON. BuildInput includes anatomical and segmentation paths, trajectory names and positions, which may contain identifiers or sensitive subject information; chmod also overrides a restrictive umask for the file.
findings.suggestion: Create or validate the sync directory as private and keep synchronization files owner-readable and writable only, ensuring the same-user BabelBrain process can still access them.

findings.title: Geometry mismatch warning is shown only after launching BabelBrain
findings.explanation: prepareT1w reports an affine mismatch that may misplace trajectories, but launch starts the external process before returning that warning. Users cannot review or cancel the mismatch before the application receives the inputs.
findings.suggestion: Validate geometry and present warnings before starting the external application, with an option to cancel.
